items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I remember this so well because in order to get the band and Joe together the scheduling was ridiculous.

ctx.x: But anyway, when we did rehearse, we’d have to rehearse like at midnight or something, because a lot of a guys had studio work in the day. Not me so much, I was never really a full time studio player. And there was a lot of work. A lot of guys were full time studio — but there was so much work that there was overflow work all the time, so then you got called by people you didn’t know lots of times because of recommendations, just to go in and deal with whatever you had to do. Very challenging stuff sometimes you…

can handle this, and you turn the page and all of a sudden you’re in another world. Maybe you’re playing alone with a harp or something, you know it’s very sensitive stuff. You’ve just been playing in a circus on the page before, who knows? But getting back to this, this was really exceptional. I remember this so well because in order to get the band and Joe together the scheduling was ridiculous. It started at eight in the morning on a couple of the days and one was at seven in the morning. Now this is, for the…
I was going to think if he had just gotten out of bed for that you wouldn’t be able to hear his voice, ‘cause it’d be so low.
